chapter: Life on the road and in the Webb band's book
title: Strain at the Paramount, a late Decca session and the final illness
summary: Joe Saunders carried the exhausted Webb offstage between Paramount shows; they recorded "Spanish Tour" at night, then Webb went to Hopkins.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: Yeah. Because he used to play at the Paramount, and after the curtain he be so exhausted that Joe Saunders had to pick him up and carry him off the stage on to the elevator upstairs.
Joe Saunders was kind of a heavy set fella. Joe Saunders is about my built but a little bit heavier now.

He would just pick him up and just take him off the drums and take him up and lay him down in the dressing room. (Unaudible). Take him up and give him some kind of medicine -- get him ready for the next show.
Get enough energy and strength together,

and he'd come down for the next show. We were doing six shows in the --
That is really --
Because after that night when we finished at the Paramount, we went to Decca and we did that -- two sides there. "Spanish Tour" (Inaudible), that big record you have there.
Remember it looked like an Lp with just the two sides on it?
Oh yeah.
Well we cut that about one or two o'clock at night at Decca -- cut those two sides.
He say, "We're gonna do a recording date tonight. We're gonna cut an album." And we cut those two sides, side one and side two. Two different sides.
And we was on our way -- that's when we were getting ready to go down South -- on that trip I was telling you about.
We got to Washington, he was going back to John Hopkins Hospital, because we had just came out

of the Paramount Theater. And that's where he was very sick. He was very sick at the Paramount Theater. You wouldn't know it, because between shows they would give him something. He'd lay down and get himself together.
And he --
Courageous fellow, too.
Yeah.
And after we ready to (inaudible) go on this trip, he had decided that he was going to stop at John Hopkins Hospital for a few days, take a check-up and see what they, you know, but that was it.
The following day, something when (inaudible) he went up there, they must've tried some kind of medicine on him, or something, but he passed away.
Had an operation, they probably -- they tried to save him then.
So what was happening to him all the time probably was happening to him at the Paramount Theater.
And nobody -- we just thought maybe he was just sick and he was falling out.

What was happening to him was happening to him then -- what caused his death. Because he working and they had had that operation in New York.

Somebody had took something out of that spine or did something to it. When we went in the Paramount Theater, and whatever happened, that hard work at the Paramount Theater brought on that illness -- did something.
It caused his death, because right after that, when we got to Washington, he drove back to John Hopkins to see if he could straighten out, or something.

Yeah, I think the part where -- Yeah, I think that strain, you know, that strain from the Paramount really brought that on.
